clue.text: Beef or fish

definitions.meaning: to beef is to complain or grumble, slang verb
a freshwater fish common in ponds and lakes

explanation.walkthrough: 'Beef' looks like a noun for meat beside 'fish', but it is the slang verb for grumbling.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: a verb meaning to grumble or find fault, and the name of a freshwater fish species.

clue.text: Expert before the judge seen to go to pieces

parts.note: crack means expert, first-rate, as in a crack shot
to be up before the judge is to appear in court

explanation.surface: A skilled defendant breaks down when brought into court.
explanation.definitionFit: To crack up is to suffer a breakdown, losing composure under strain.

clue.text: Person whose relations are said to be interesting

definitions.text: Person whose relations are said to be interesting

parts.words: Person whose relations are said to be interesting
parts.note: reads as someone with fascinating relatives, but relations here are things related, stories told

explanation.definitionFit: A skilled storyteller, someone whose recounted tales are entertaining to hear.

clue.text: Sales patter given by fellow always in state of great excitement

parts.note: ever means always, as in 'for ever'
a salesman's pitch is the patter used to sell

explanation.surface: A salesman's spiel delivered by someone who is perpetually worked up.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: a fever pitch is the height of excitement or agitation.

clue.text: Industrial area south of centre of Leeds, say

indicators.note: in a down clue, south of means the following word sits below the letter
centre of picks the middle letter of the city name

parts.note: to state is to say

explanation.surface: A factory district lying to the south of central Leeds.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry, 'south of' puts STATE beneath E, the middle letter of LEEDS.
explanation.definitionFit: An industrial estate is a zone set aside for factories and businesses.

clue.text: Drinks machine in The Times press office

indicators.note: in means the letters are found within the run of words

explanation.surface: A coffee maker installed in the newspaper's printing office.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The Times' looks like the paper's name, but its end letters start the run.
explanation.definitionFit: An espresso is a machine that forces steam through ground coffee to make strong coffee.

clue.text: Business of soldiers individually and collectively

parts.note: a single soldier of the lowest rank is a private
a company is a unit of soldiers taken together

explanation.surface: The affairs of troops, both one by one and as a group.
explanation.definitionFit: A private company is a business whose shares are not traded publicly.

clue.text: Twit getting tight around end of afternoon

indicators.note: around means the tight word encloses the letter

parts.note: taut means pulled tight

indicators.note: end of picks the last letter of the word

explanation.surface: A fool who gets drunk by late afternoon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Twit' looks like a noun for a fool but is the verb meaning to tease; 'tight' is not drunk but taut.
explanation.definitionFit: To twit someone is to tease or mock them, much as one would jeer.

clue.text: Expression of astonishment coming out of the blue

definitions.meaning: an exclamation of surprise, like 'good gracious!'
the blue is the sky, the firmament above

explanation.walkthrough: 'coming out of' links the two senses and suggests a surprise from nowhere.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: an exclamation of surprise, and the sky or firmament overhead.

clue.text: Do I function too poorly, being unfit

indicators.note: poorly means badly made, so the letters are put together another way

explanation.surface: Someone asking whether they work too badly, being out of shape.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: to be out of condition is to be physically unfit.

clue.text: History books

definitions.meaning: a history is a narrative record of events, a chronicle
the books of a business are its financial records

explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: a narrative report of events, and a financial record kept by a business or bank.

clue.text: Wet soil, mostly during April, ruined plant

indicators.note: during means the soil piece sits within the rearranged month
ruined means the letters of April are wrecked and rebuilt in a new order
mostly means the last letter of the soil word is dropped

parts.note: mud is wet soil

explanation.surface: Muddy ground in a wet April has spoiled a garden plant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ruined' turns the month into PRILA; the soil piece drops its last letter and sits after PRI. 'plant' is the definition, not a factory.
explanation.definitionFit: The primula is a genus of flowering plants including primroses and cowslips.

clue.text: Frequently he gets absorbed by chessmen in game

indicators.note: being absorbed by means going inside the pair of chess pieces

parts.note: the king and the castle (rook) are two chessmen
oft is an old word for often, frequently

explanation.surface: A man who keeps getting lost in thought over his chess pieces during a game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'chessmen' supplies two separate pieces that together surround the inserted words; the game is the children's one of defending a mound.
explanation.definitionFit: A children's game in which one player holds a mound against others trying to push them off.

clue.text: Riddle posed by Queen in newspaper article?

indicators.note: in means the royal abbreviation goes inside the article word

parts.note: a piece is an article written for a newspaper
R, for Regina, is the crossword abbreviation for a queen

explanation.surface: A puzzle set by the monarch appearing in a newspaper feature.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Riddle' looks like a puzzle noun but is the verb meaning to fill with holes.
explanation.definitionFit: To riddle something is to perforate it with many holes, as bullets do; to pierce is to puncture.

clue.text: An alarming message about extremely risky material

parts.note: an gives the indefinite article A

indicators.note: about means the distress call goes round the next word

parts.note: SOS is the international distress signal
best can mean to the highest degree, most, extremely

explanation.surface: A frightening warning concerning a highly dangerous substance.
explanation.definitionFit: Asbestos is a fibrous mineral once used for insulation, now known as a serious health hazard.

clue.text: Disagree with children's conduct at first

indicators.note: at first means the conduct word is placed before the offspring word

parts.note: to take someone somewhere is to conduct them
issue means offspring, children

explanation.surface: Objecting to the way youngsters behave initially.
explanation.walkthrough: 'conduct' looks like a noun for behaviour but is the verb to lead, TAKE.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: to take issue is to dispute or object.

clue.text: Get on with extremely peculiar, bad-tempered woman

indicators.note: extremely means the outermost letters of the word are taken

parts.note: an ogress is a fierce, frightening woman

explanation.surface: Get along with a decidedly odd, cantankerous woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extremely' gives P and R, the first and last letters of 'peculiar'.
explanation.definitionFit: To progress is to advance or get on, as in making progress at work.

clue.text: Ratings could have risen possibly at end of short month

indicators.note: placed at the end of means the rearranged letters follow the month

parts.note: Mar is the abbreviation of March

indicators.note: possibly signals the letters of risen could be arranged another way

explanation.surface: Viewing figures might have climbed towards the close of a brief month.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ratings' looks like viewing figures but means ordinary sailors.
explanation.definitionFit: In the navy, ratings are sailors below officer rank, and mariners are seamen.

clue.text: Elder brother going on about holiday resort

indicators.note: in a down clue, going on means the next piece is added below

parts.note: in British schools the older of two brothers is called major
ca, for circa, means about

explanation.surface: An older sibling chatting about a trip abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: In British public schools the elder of two brothers is Smith major, the younger Smith minor.
explanation.definitionFit: Majorca is a Spanish Mediterranean island popular with tourists, an example of a resort.

clue.text: Cargo handler's consignment note finally amended

indicators.note: finally amended means the last letter of the note word is changed for another

parts.note: a docket is a document listing goods in a consignment

explanation.surface: A dock worker's delivery note has been corrected at the end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finally amended' changes the final T of DOCKET; the replacement R is not clued, only implied by the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A docker is a labourer who loads and unloads ships at a port.

clue.text: Withdraw troops over extended area

indicators.note: in a down clue, over means the first piece sits above the second

parts.note: RE, the Royal Engineers, is a common crossword abbreviation for troops
a tract is a large stretch of land

explanation.surface: Soldiers pull back across a wide expanse of territory.
explanation.definitionFit: To retract is to take back or withdraw a statement or claw.

clue.text: What primarily amorous lover may make you

definitions.text: What primarily amorous lover may make you

indicators.note: primarily means the first letter of the word

parts.note: an old flame is a former lover

explanation.surface: How a passionate partner may leave you feeling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'amorous' gives its first letter A; a flame is a sweetheart.
explanation.definitionFit: Being aflame means burning with passion, as an ardent sweetheart might leave you.

clue.text: The start of spring?

parts.note: reads as the beginning of a season, but means the place where one starts a leap

explanation.definitionFit: A starting place for any venture, playfully read as the spot one leaps from.

clue.text: Rise and fall of a precocious schoolgirl?

indicators.note: in a down entry, rise and fall means it reads the same upward and downward

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.surface: The ups and downs of a cheeky young pupil.
explanation.walkthrough: A palindrome reads the same up or down the grid; a madam is a cheeky, forward girl.
explanation.definitionFit: Madam is a British colloquial term for a precocious, bossy or cheeky girl.

clue.text: Tent, say, left — new one abandoned?

parts.note: red means politically left-wing

indicators.note: abandoned, meaning wild and unrestrained, signals the letters are jumbled

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A camper's shelter left behind, with a new one discarded.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tent' is not a shelter but a deep red Spanish wine; 'abandoned' rearranges NEW plus I into WINE.
explanation.definitionFit: Tent is a dark red Spanish wine, so it is an example of the drink.

clue.text: Memory loss affected men in wide area of continent

indicators.note: in means the rearranged letters sit inside the continent

parts.note: Asia is the largest continent, a vast area

indicators.note: affected means the letters of men are altered in order

explanation.surface: Forgetfulness afflicted men across a vast stretch of a landmass.
explanation.walkthrough: 'affected' jumbles 'men' into MNE; 'wide area of continent' is just a roundabout name for the largest continent.
explanation.definitionFit: Amnesia is the medical term for partial or total loss of memory.

clue.text: Given little notice, clergyman had to manage

parts.note: an ad is a short advertisement, a small notice
a minister is a member of the clergy

explanation.surface: A vicar told at short notice that he must cope.
explanation.definitionFit: To administer is to run or manage affairs, as in administering an estate.

clue.text: Master's cane

definitions.meaning: to master an opponent is to defeat or overcome them
to cane is to thrash or strike with a stick

explanation.definitionFit: Two verb senses: to defeat an opponent, and to strike repeatedly as a punishment.
